chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Denmark with John Darville and tenor Jesper Thilo
summary: He toured Denmark, played the Montmartre, and praises tenor Jesper Thilo.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, well he's French but he's livin' over there, so. I made a very nice recording called "Swinging the Blues" with all of these fellows. Then I went to Denmark and I played with John Darville there.
DARVILLE. I played there with him and we toured all over Denmark and we played in the Montmartre which is a club, a jazz club.
Yes. I enjoyed that quite a bit. Quite a bit! He's got a saxophone player there Jesper Tylo. Thilo.
Jesper is spelled JESPER TYLO. Jesper Tylo. Beautiful, one of the best tenor players that I've ever heard really.
Yes sir. He came to New York and broke it up down at the Straw Hat. You know, down on 49th Street.
What did you say his second name was?
Yes, he upset the whole place but he just came over here to visit New York and he had to go right, he does a lot of studio work in Denmark.
Oh, what does he sound like? Is he sort of Hawkish?
He sounds like Wardell Gray used to sound. That type.

Fast and beautiful swing. Just starved all the musicians over there. But it was nice working with him. And Henri Myer was the band leader along with John Darville, he's d trumpet players. He was here for the jazz festival.
